"Some have mentioned smell and although its true that jack olantern mushrooms have a much more powerful and traditional mushroom smell compared to the light fruity smell of chanterelles, Im not sure how reliable of character this is depending on age and species. HTTPURL"

"The spacing of these mushrooms is also helpful as chanterelles form beneficial mycorrhizal partnerships with tree roots and can be found individually protruding from soil (left 📸) vs. jacks (right 📸) which fruit in clumps on decaying (sometimes buried) wood substrates & logs. HTTPURL"
"Heres some additional 📸 of the irregular wavy margin of edible chanterelles! HTTPURL"

"Another helpful character when both are not too young or overly mature is "cap" shape. Chanterelles have a very irregular fragile margin (right in both 📸) while jacks (left in both 📸) tend to be rounder and more traditionally mushroom-shaped (round cap with narrow stalk)! HTTPURL"

"But one of the biggest differences between poisonous Jack olantern mushrooms & edible chanterelles are the gills. Gills are very pronounced & brittle on jack olanterns (left 📸whereas they are flat to almost smooth ridges on chanterelles (right 📸) that cannot be rubbed away! HTTPURL"
"The real problem is that young Jack olantern mushrooms can also look more like chanterelles especially if growing in less dense clumps or if wood substrate is hidden! HTTPURL"

"The ️ jack olantern is named as such because it glows in the dark. This waxy / shiny mushroom grows in large clumps on dead & decaying wood. Its gills are deep, fleshy, & orange & can be easily rubbed off. In old age, it can take on the shape of a chanterelle but bigger! HTTPURL"

"So I will reiterate that you should never eat something for which you are confident in its ID, I think its important to provide guidance in the event of an assumed mistaken ID. Lets focus on the poisonous look-alike, the jack olantern mushroom 🎃🍄 (Omphalotus spp.)! HTTPURL"

"Foraging for and eating wild mushrooms  is not something you should do without the guidance from an experienced forager as fungus color, shape, & timing of fruiting among other things can vary significantly, which can make ID difficult! Chanterelles vary considerably! HTTPURL"

"🚨IMPORTANT PSA🚨 Chanterelles (edible) & jack olantern mushrooms (poisonous) are both found growing this time of year & are often confused because of similarity in coloring, shape, & habitat. A lot of people end up sick & often require 🏥. Read this 🧵! HTTPURL"

"Id like to thank those who I reached out to privately for feedback on the first drafts of my article. I owe each of you a debt of gratitude 🙏!  22/n"

"At the end of the day Im just an imperfect fun guy with #ADHD & #GAD. Ill be highlighting some of my continuing struggles and successes living with these disorders under #FungiWithADHD if you interested in following my journey. 21/n"

"Many scientists, particularly early- career scientists, continue to suffer in silence with the perpetual fear of having their mental illness outed. This is for you. You are not alone. You matter tremendously to me & others. Its never to late to seek out professional help. 20/n"

"Im no longer hiding. Being open about my own mental disorder doesnt diminish my value & contributions as a scientist. The contributions & perspectives of neurodivergent scientists, including many reading this, enrich academia and contribute to a healthier environment! 19/n"

"My #ADHD & #GAD dont simply end with medication & therapy. Ive been so inspired by @USER  @USER @USER @USER @USER & others who tirelessly advocate to normalize mental illness & promote #AcademicMentalHealth!  🙏! 18/n"

"In hindsight my diagnosis of #ADHD & #GAD makes a lot of sense. And let me say there were tons of mixed feelings about my diagnosis. These disorders may be less stigmatized compared to other mental disorders but they are serious life-altering disorders nonetheless. 17/n"

"I vividly recall last June / July hitting a wall. I wandered around our university farm woodlot every day (sometimes several times a day) with my 5-year old collecting millipedes because I couldnt get out of that pattern as I had no more coping mechanisms to function. 15/n"

"At first the surge of anxiety accelerated my productivity. But this productivity was short lived as my coping mechanisms could no longer function and support the weight of my crumbling mental health. 14/n"

"I think it was clear to everyone around me that something had changed. Something was broken. I used our universitys faculty / staff assistance program to see a therapist and get a referral for a psychiatrist (an impossible task during a pandemic). 16/n"

"But heres the catch with my #ADHD, all the lanes are all hyperfocused on research with no executive function available for administrative tasks or personal things. The pandemic changed all that and something big had to give and that something was me. 12/n"

"As the dad & primary parent (my partner is a physician w/ less flexibility in her work schedule) of 3 young boys, I took on overseeing at home care & virtual schooling from 3/2020 to 8/2021. This was on top of virtual teaching for @USER & running my lab. 13/n"

"My mind is like a 15 lane superhighway & each lane represents a different project in my lab. If one lane slows due to bottlenecks, Ill switch lanes to maintain speed. My brain needs constant stimulation. If all lanes slow, I add more lanes. I assumed expansion was infinite 11/n"

"I finished my PhD in 2012 & after a 2-year post-doc, I took my current position as faculty at @USER. Another unexpected thing happened in my first years as a first time faculty member. My need for tons of external stimuli to calm my brain was surprisingly satisfied. 10/n"

"I wasnt trying to tough it out. I knew deep down I wasnt bipolar, which was hard because it had become part of my identity. But the costs of self neglect are incalculable to me, my partner @USER & my family. Ive spent a lot of time in therapy unpacking all that. 9/n"

"I think an important thing to bring up here is that even though #ADHD & #GAD are treatable & have quite a few options regarding medications, I was undiagnosed and unmedicated for 17 years without any therapy except for my ad-hoc coping mechanisms. 8/n"

"Looking back I think things were far worse for me mentally during my PhD, which manifested as obsessive hyperfocus on my dissertation work. I recall going back into the lab after my partner and I brought our first born home the hospital. That fact still kills me 7/n"

"As I encountered hurdles in dealing with my mental illness, I developed ad-hoc coping mechanisms, some of which falsely reassured me I didnt need outside help. I finished my B.S. in 2005 & my M.S. in 2007. I started my PhD in Plant Pathology in fall 2007. 6/n"

"In 2003, I returned to the university & turned my anxiety & hyperfocus (a confusing symptom some of us with #adhd experience) to the study of fungi. I pulled consecutive all night work sessions & generated tons of data. On the inside I was emotionally unstable & isolated. 5/n"

"But something unexpected happened and it took me two decades to actually make sense of it. My depression never returned, but the anxiety and hyperactivity (masquerading as hypomania) metastasized. In hindsight its clear that my initial diagnosis of bipolar  was incorrect. 4/n"
